decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 3.75% to 4%. The vote was 10-2. Dissenting: Stephen I. Miran, Jeffrey R. Schmid.

changes.quote: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year.”

changes.quote: Job gains have slowed this year, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remained low through August; more recent indicators are consistent with these developments.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low.”

changes.quote: Inflation has moved up since earlier in the year and remains somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has moved up and remains somewhat elevated.”

changes.quote: The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment have risen.”

tone_quotes.quote: In support of its goals and in light of the shift in the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.
Inflation has moved up since earlier in the year and remains somewhat elevated.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 21.16% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.08% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.27% would rise by about $17.61 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of 23k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3% over the past year (September 2025); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.9% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +12 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 35%, cut 65%, hike 0%.
